T0605.title: Embodied Intelligence
T0605.definition: An intelligent-agent system with a physical body and perception-decision capability that perceives the environment via sensors and acts on it via actuators in the physical world, covering humanoid robots, service robots, and autonomous-driving embodied systems.
T0605.description: Embodied intelligence is an intersection of AI and robotics, emphasizing intelligence achieved through physical-body interaction with the environment. Unlike traditional software AI (e.g., large language models running only in digital space), embodied-intelligence decisions translate directly into physical actions and are irreversible. Its tech stack includes multi-modal perception (vision, language, touch), VLA-model decision-making, and motion planning and execution. Embodied intelligence faces unique security risks: VLA model adversarial attacks, teleoperation hijacking, robot physical harm, and physical-world prompt injection — these risks are harder to defend than pure software AI and have more severe consequences due to physical-world involvement.
T0605.usageExample: An embodied-intelligence robot in a warehouse perceives goods and performs grasping via a VLA model; once the model is adversarially attacked, it may grab the wrong item or even strike people.
